senses.gloss:
Luśa is represented in a series of passages in the Brāhmaṇas as a rival of kutsa for the favour of indra. To luśa Dhānāka the authorship of certain hymns is ascribed by the Anukramaṇī (Index) of the Rigveda.
Foot notes pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, ix. 2, 22; Jaiminīya brāhmaṇa, i. 128; Śāṭyāyanaka in Oertel, Journal of the American Oriental Society, 18, 31 et seq.
x. 35. 36. Cf. Bṛhaddevatā, ii. 129; iii. 55, with Macdonell's notes.
Cf. Hillebrandt, Vedische Mythologie, 3, 291, n. 3; Lévi, La Doctrine du Sacrifice, 37, 38.

Luśākapi Khārgali (‘descendant of Khṛgala’) is mentioned in the pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa as having cursed kuṣītaka and the Kauṣītakins. He was a contemporary of keśin dālbhya according to the kāṭhaka Saṃhitā.
Foot notes xvii. 4, 3. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 10, 145, n. 3.
xxx. 2 (Indische Studien, 3, 471); Kapiṣṭhala Saṃhitā, xlvi. 5.
